blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Fine‑Tuning Wins—A Beginner’s Guide to Preserving Knowledge in Foundation Models
blogs.description: Demystify the core idea behind orthogonal fine‑tuning (OFT): how a single orthogonal matrix preserves the geometric structure of a pre‑trained model’s weights, keeping its learned knowledge intact while adapting to new tasks. We’ll explain pair‑wise angles, spectral norms, and why this simple multiplicative update outperforms naive parameter tweaks.

blogs.title: Butterfly Matrices: The Secret Sauce for Tiny but Powerful Finetuning
blogs.description: Explore the Cooley‑Tukey butterfly structure that lets us factor a huge dense orthogonal matrix into a handful of sparse blocks. We’ll walk through the math in plain language, show how this reduces trainable parameters from O(d²) to O(d log d), and give hands‑on examples of building these matrices in NumPy or PyTorch.

blogs.title: From Diffusion Models to Vision Transformers: How BOFT Adapts Any Large Model
blogs.description: Take a tour of Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) across diverse domains—text‑to‑image Diffusers, Vision Transformers, and LLMs. The post will cover experimental results, why BOFT outperforms LoRA and other PEFT methods, and the practical steps needed to plug BOFT into existing pipelines.

blogs.title: Parameter Efficiency vs Expressivity: Striking the Right Balance in Model Tuning
blogs.description: Delve into the trade‑off between keeping fine‑tuning parameters small and maintaining enough flexibility to reach the target task. We’ll discuss block‑diagonal OFT vs BOFT, explain expressivity theorems, and give guidelines for choosing block sizes and depth for your own models.

blogs.title: Dropout Reimagined: Multiplicative Dropout for Butterfly‑Based Fine‑Tuning
blogs.description: Standard dropout is ill‑suited for multiplicative updates like BOFT. Learn how multiplicative dropout randomly masks butterfly components during training, keeps inference latency at zero, and helps prevent over‑fitting on low‑data regimes.
